review_notes: I read the whole file and the underlying tensorMapCLM lemmas in AlgebraicDirectLimits/Topology/TensorProduct.lean, and grepped for uses of the simp lemmas. I did not run Lean, so the claim that these simp lemmas never fire rests on how simp rewrites subterms before enclosing terms. The simp attributes on _obj and _map_hom look right. The rest of the interface (map_id, map_comp, additivity) uses the standard Functor and Additive API. I found no loop and no competing rules.

findings.excerpt:
((tensorLeftFunctor R C).map g).hom.toLinearMap =
      TensorProduct.map (LinearMap.id : C →ₗ[R] C) g.hom.toLinearMap
findings.problem: Both lemmas carry @[simp] but sit downstream of the simp lemma tensorLeftFunctor_map_hom. Each left-hand side contains the subterm `((tensorLeftFunctor R C).map g).hom`. Simp normally rewrites subterms before the enclosing term, so that subterm should become `tensorMapCLM R id g.hom` first. The outer pattern `….hom.toLinearMap` (or `….hom (c ⊗ₜ m)`) then no longer matches syntactically. The existing simp lemmas tensorMapCLM_toLinearMap and tensorMapCLM_tmul already finish the job from the tensorMapCLM form. So these two @[simp] attributes are probably dead rules. They add simp-set size and give a misleading impression of a second normal form. The only outside use I found (AlgebraicDirectLimitsExamples/TensorFunctor.lean:236) cites tensorLeftFunctor_map_tmul by name.
findings.proposed_change: Keep tensorLeftFunctor_map_hom as the single simp rewrite out of the functor. It leads into the tensorMapCLM normal form, which tensorMapCLM_toLinearMap and tensorMapCLM_tmul already handle. Drop @[simp] from tensorLeftFunctor_map_toLinearMap and tensorLeftFunctor_map_tmul, and keep them as plain theorems for explicit `rw` or `exact`. Alternatively, make the shortcuts fire first by marking them `@[simp↓]`. The first option is simpler.
findings.benefit: The simp interface gets one canonical entry point, with no redundant rules that cannot fire. Readers see the intended normal form, `tensorMapCLM` followed by `TensorProduct.map` or `tmul`, without wondering which of several overlapping lemmas applies. The named lemmas stay available for the example file.

evidence.excerpt: (tensorMapCLM R f g).toLinearMap = TensorProduct.map f g.toLinearMap := rfl
tensorMapCLM R f g (c ⊗ₜ[R] m) = f c ⊗ₜ[R] g m

((tensorLeftFunctor R C).map g).hom =
      tensorMapCLM R (LinearMap.id : C →ₗ[R] C) g.hom
